title: District 8 forum turns heated over downtown tax as Treviño and Lopez split
excerpt: At a District 8 candidate forum on Nov. 12, Priscilla Treviño blasted the downtown assessment she calls the 'Cigarroa tax,' while Irma Lopez warned against dissolving the funding for downtown improvements.
content:
The race for Laredo's District 8 council seat turned sharp at a candidate forum on Wednesday, Nov. 12, 2026, as the candidates split over the future of downtown and the assessment that pays for its improvements.

Priscilla Treviño, also known as La Gordiloca, argued the additional downtown assessment — which she called the "Cigarroa tax" — discourages investment and adds another burden on property owners who already pay regular taxes. She said downtown investors were benefiting while ordinary residents kept struggling, and she called for filling vacant buildings, bringing businesses back downtown, and revisiting a proposed children's museum she said outgoing Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa had rejected.

Irma Lopez, a teacher of 33 years, took the opposite view. She said she had reviewed an upcoming City Council agenda and found an item — Item 67 — dealing with dissolving the downtown assessment. Lopez questioned why the city would consider ending a funding mechanism meant to pay for sidewalks, trees, and other downtown infrastructure, and asked what would happen to that money and whether taxpayers would end up covering the costs.

The dispute centers on the Central Laredo Municipal Management District's Business Improvement District assessment, an additional charge on qualifying downtown properties. The district was created by the Texas Legislature in 2013 and is authorized to levy assessments for downtown improvements; state law also allows the City of Laredo to dissolve it.

Cigarroa is leaving the District 8 seat to run for mayor, putting her downtown record in the spotlight as voters choose her successor.

Source: Hammrod News Laredo TX video of the City District 8 Forum, Nov. 12, 2026.
